I'm wary of site-wide filters or special algorithms because you have to remember that it will affect Reddit-specific subverses like /v/meanwhileonreddit. I also don't believe that we should be curating content on a site level, only at the subverse level according to the rules and community of the subverse. Most of Reddit's problems come from trying to control content site-wide, and it's just not the way the subreddit system was designed. If you're talking about just /v/news, my suggestion would be to treat news about Reddit as if you were writing the article yourself. Are you writing it to be news for the general public, or are you writing it to appeal to ex and current redditors? If it's general interest, then upvote it. If it's special interest for ex and current redditors, then it's probably not pertinent to /v/news. Make it a guideline, sure. I'd hesitate to make it a hard and fast rule, because I still think upvotes/downvotes should curate content. The community has to take some responsibility for the quality of its subverse, or else it's going to balk when changes are implemented for it. And it's my position that Voat shouldn't be curating content site-wide. Voat should take action against unlawful content, allow lawful content to be moderated by the subverses themselves, and give users the power to block what subverses they find unpleasant without banning the subverse. It seems like the best way to run a free system, and it's what Reddit almost pulled off before going heavy on the site-wide content curating.
